brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: 3 full-hex cells over 2 storeys with solid top covers forming a shelf deck (deck f22), joint bolts and end caps; book-row and book props staged on top. But parts are 3D-printed plastic in a user-chosen material and the configurator checks fit/collisions only, so no load rating can be verified.
requirements.requirement: Shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books

requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,1#cut on piece:0,1,0;half-n and drawer:0#-1,1#cut on piece:-1,1,0;half-n; both topped with half-n covers.
Top-deck shelf surfaces (f22 deck across 3 covers) hold book-row prop:1 and book prop:2; check_build ok with meshClash clear.
requirements.requirement: Shelf function for books (visible, verified build)

finish.summary: Built a low 2-storey shelf (3 full cells) with two half-base drawers alongside, solid covers as shelf decks, joint bolts and end caps, dressed with books. Load rating cannot be verified: 50 kg rating is unmet by the configurator (plastic parts, fit-check only); the low, bolted form only partly addresses it.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: 50-kg rating can't be verified in plastic — I'll still build you a sturdy shelf with two drawers.
